Modern sequence models are increasingly deployed as agents that interleave token generation with calls to external tools. We model finite-precision state-space models with $B$ bits of internal state. Every finite-state bounded-interface tool with memory set $M$ can be internalized at a cost of at most $\lceil\log_2 |M|\rceil + O(1)$ recurrent bits. A single unbounded tape with only local $\mathtt{read}$/$\mathtt{write}$/$\mathtt{move}$ commands suffices for Turing completeness: every single-tape Turing machine with state set $Q$ and tape alphabet $\Gamma$ is simulated by a controller with $O(\log |Q| + \log |\Gamma|)$ recurrent bits, and $EQ_n$ requires $2^n$ states without tools. Under explicitly stated resource conventions, $O(\log B)$ recurrent bits suffice for tape-assisted simulation of any $B$-state Turing machine, whereas directly realizing an arbitrary $B$-state transition map requires total recurrent dimension exactly $B-1$.
